terms.gloss: represent, portray, model (in a statue or a picture)
terms.comment: Properly “press out”, and so “model” in wax, clay or bronze; Lewis & Short: in this sense mostly poetic and post-Augustan, frequent in the elder Pliny. Of a likeness: imāginem alicujus exprimere.

evidence: Verg. A. 6.32: cāsūs effingere in aurō

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: in this sense post-Augustan. Not for acting on someone’s behalf (see represent, act or speak for).

phrases.latin: Aemilium circā lūdum faber īmus et unguīs exprimet et mollīs imitābitur aere capillōs
phrases.english: the humblest bronze-smith by the Aemilian school will render the nails and copy soft hair in bronze

phrases.latin: bis cōnātus erat cāsūs effingere in aurō; bis patriae cecidēre manūs
phrases.english: twice he had tried to portray the fall in gold; twice the father’s hands dropped

sources: Lewis & Short: exprimo · Lewis & Short: effingo · Lewis & Short: repraesento
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. represent.
Horace, Ars poetica, and Vergil, Aeneid 6, checked against the Perseus Latin texts and the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
